story: Meera’s SYNTHETIC rentals are r1: 2 days at 8 units per day and r2: 3 days at 5. The hand total is 16 + 15 = 31 fictional units. A notebook is a document mixing code and explanation. A code cell is one block you can run separately; its kernel is the running process that executes it and remembers values. Her displayed cell A calculates costs from tickets, while displayed cell B defines tickets. Earlier she ran B, then A printed total units: 31. The kernel kept tickets from that earlier run: hidden state is remembered information the displayed execution order does not supply.

Restarting the kernel clears that memory. Running the displayed A first now ends with NameError: name 'tickets' is not defined; NameError reports that a required name is unavailable. A virtual environment, or venv, is a project directory with its own Python entry point and package installation area. A package is installed reusable code; pip is the installer run through the chosen interpreter. A pinned version such as numpy==2.3.5 asks for that exact release. requirements.txt lists requested packages; python3 -m venv .venv creates the environment, and .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt installs those requests there. The -m option runs a named Python module; -r reads the requirements file. pip freeze lists installed package versions. Using the explicit .venv/bin/python path selects the environment without relying on an activated shell. The tiny script needs no extra package; the pins support the notebook tools and separate data-lab practice.

Git records selected file contents. The working tree is the editable set of files on disk; staged content is the version selected for the next saved snapshot, called a commit. git status shows file states; git diff shows tracked edits not yet staged. git add rental_summary.py selects that file’s current contents; git diff --staged shows the selected changes before git commit saves them locally. Here --unified=0 omits unchanged context lines from the diff and --name-only lists paths. A .gitignore file tells Git which untracked paths to leave out of normal status and staging. The .venv/ directory and .env secret file belong outside the snapshot. Ignoring a file does not remove an already tracked copy or erase a leaked secret.

mechanism: Reproduction needs both an execution order and a recorded environment. The repaired notebook defines tickets before calculating costs; the script makes the function’s input explicit and checks the hand total. Merely exporting cells into a .py file preserves their bad order unless you repair it. Remove notebook-only commands and stale outputs, then run the file in a new process. The -I option requests Python’s isolated mode, reducing reliance on user-site packages and Python environment variables; it does not create a venv or remove dependencies you import.

An environment specification and an installed snapshot answer different questions. The requirements file asks for selected versions. pip freeze records what pip sees installed, including additional packages resolved for those requests. Save the full output, not just the five lines displayed here. These direct pins and this local snapshot are not a complete cross-platform lockfile. Record the interpreter and kernel too: a notebook can connect to a Python other than the one whose pip you just used. The practice diagnostic uses sys.executable, the interpreter’s path, and importlib.metadata.version, which reads an installed package’s version.

topics.title: running scripts versus notebooks
topics.explanation: Notebook cells send code to a persistent kernel, so rerunning, moving or editing cells can leave memory that the displayed text does not explain. A saved output can outlive the state that produced it. Restart and run in displayed order before sharing a result. Running python3 -I rental_summary.py starts a fresh interpreter process; the script prints the actual Python version each time. The authoring environment used Python 3.12.13 and ipykernel 6.30.1. topics.title: notebook-to-script conversion
topics.explanation: Start with the repaired cell order, move imports and inputs before their uses, put the calculation in a function with explicit arguments, and remove notebook-only commands. topics.title: Git basics for one file
topics.explanation: git status --short shows two state columns: staged first, working-tree second. The practice changes an already tracked file, so git diff shows it before staging; an untracked new file would not appear in that diff. git add selects the current contents, and git diff --staged compares that selection with the last commit. --name-only lists staged paths. Ignored paths do not include secrets in a snapshot, but ignoring is not encryption and does not untrack existing files. A local commit does not publish or push anything.
